/**
* Hands the device's own effect panel this app's audio session.
*
* Shared with [EqualizerScreen], which offers the same escape hatch a second
* time next to the equaliser it might be an alternative to.
*/
internal fun openEqualizer(context: Context, sessionId: Int) {
val intent = Intent(AudioEffect.ACTION_DISPLAY_AUDIO_EFFECT_CONTROL_PANEL).apply {
putExtra(AudioEffect.EXTRA_AUDIO_SESSION, sessionId)
putExtra(AudioEffect.EXTRA_PACKAGE_NAME, context.packageName)
putExtra(AudioEffect.EXTRA_CONTENT_TYPE, AudioEffect.CONTENT_TYPE_MUSIC)
}
runCatching { context.startActivity(intent) }.onFailure {
Toast.makeText(context, context.getString(R.string.no_equalizer), Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
}
}

/** Above this, the cache limit slider's subtitle warns rather than reassures. */
private const val CACHE_WARNING_MB = 2048

/**
* Where the cache limit slider's "Unlimited" stop sits: one 512MB step past
* [AppSettings.MAX_CACHE_LIMIT_BYTES], so the fixed sizes keep their positions.
*/
private const val CACHE_UNLIMITED_STOP_MB = 10 * 1024 + 512

/** "512 MB", "2 GB", "2.5 GB" — whichever reads more naturally at that size. */
private fun formatCacheSize(mb: Int): String {
if (mb < 1024) return "$mb MB"
val gb = mb / 1024f
return if (gb == gb.toInt().toFloat()) "${gb.toInt()} GB" else "%.1f GB".format(Locale.ROOT, gb)
}

/** "850 KB", "42.3 MB", "1.20 GB" — the exact size stored, finer than [formatCacheSize]. */
private fun formatStoredBytes(bytes: Long): String {
val kb = bytes / 1024.0
val mb = kb / 1024.0
val gb = mb / 1024.0
return when {
gb >= 1.0 -> "%.2f GB".format(Locale.ROOT, gb)
mb >= 1.0 -> "%.1f MB".format(Locale.ROOT, mb)
kb >= 1.0 -> "%.0f KB".format(Locale.ROOT, kb)
else -> "$bytes B"
}
}

/**
* A setting the bit-perfect output bypasses, faded and closed to touch while
* that output is ready. With the mode on but its DAC unplugged the setting
* works, and looks it.
*
* Only the touches that would change something are taken, so the page still
* scrolls when a swipe starts on one of these rows: the press and the
* release (no ripple, no click, no switch flip) and a sideways drag (no
* slider). A vertical drag is left alone, and the list's scrolling still
* starts from a press that was taken, so it scrolls as from any other row.
*/
@Composable
private fun BypassedByBitPerfect(bypassed: Boolean, content: @Composable () -> Unit) {
val alpha by animateFloatAsState(if (bypassed) 0.38f else 1f, label = "bypassed")
// A Column, not a Box: a row can be several stacked pieces (a title row
// and its control), and a Box would draw them over one another.
Column(
Modifier
.alpha(alpha)
.then(
if (bypassed) {
Modifier.pointerInput(Unit) {
awaitEachGesture {
awaitFirstDown(requireUnconsumed = false, pass = PointerEventPass.Initial).consume()
var sideways: Boolean? = null
var travel = Offset.Zero
do {
val event = awaitPointerEvent(PointerEventPass.Initial)
event.changes.forEach { change ->
when {
change.changedToUpIgnoreConsumed() -> change.consume()
change.positionChanged() -> {
travel += change.positionChange()
if (sideways == null && travel.getDistance() > viewConfiguration.touchSlop / 2) {
sideways = abs(travel.x) > abs(travel.y)
}
if (sideways == true) change.consume()
}
}
}
} while (event.changes.any { it.pressed })
}
}
} else {
Modifier
},
),
) {
content()
}
}

@Composable
private fun BitPerfectMode.localizedLabel(): String = stringResource(
when (this) {
BitPerfectMode.OFF -> R.string.off
BitPerfectMode.USB_ANDROID -> R.string.bit_perfect_mode_usb_android
BitPerfectMode.DAP_EXCLUSIVE -> R.string.bit_perfect_mode_dap_exclusive
BitPerfectMode.USB_DIRECT -> R.string.bit_perfect_mode_usb_direct
},
)

/** Whether this phone can use [this] at all, independent of what is plugged in. */
private val BitPerfectMode.isSupported: Boolean
get() = when (this) {
BitPerfectMode.OFF -> true
BitPerfectMode.USB_ANDROID -> Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 34
BitPerfectMode.DAP_EXCLUSIVE -> Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 27
BitPerfectMode.USB_DIRECT -> true
}

@Composable
private fun BitPerfectMode.description(): String = stringResource(
when {
this == BitPerfectMode.USB_ANDROID && !isSupported -> R.string.bit_perfect_requires_android_14
this == BitPerfectMode.DAP_EXCLUSIVE && !isSupported -> R.string.bit_perfect_requires_android_8_1
this == BitPerfectMode.OFF -> R.string.bit_perfect_mode_off_subtitle
this == BitPerfectMode.USB_ANDROID -> R.string.bit_perfect_mode_usb_android_subtitle
this == BitPerfectMode.USB_DIRECT -> R.string.bit_perfect_mode_usb_direct_subtitle
else -> R.string.bit_perfect_mode_dap_exclusive_subtitle
},
)

/**
* What the exclusive output is doing now, rather than what was asked of it:
* a mode can be on while the playing track still goes through the mixer.
*/
@Composable
private fun bitPerfectSubtitle(mode: BitPerfectMode, status: BitPerfectOutput.Status): String = when {
mode == BitPerfectMode.OFF || !mode.isSupported -> mode.description()
status.active && status.dacLimited -> stringResource(
R.string.bit_perfect_status_dac_limited,
status.deviceName.orEmpty(),
"%.1f".format(status.sampleRateHz / 1000.0),
status.outputBits,
)
status.active && !status.exact -> stringResource(
R.string.bit_perfect_status_inexact,
status.deviceName.orEmpty(),
)
status.active -> stringResource(
R.string.bit_perfect_status_active,
status.deviceName.orEmpty(),
"%.1f".format(status.sampleRateHz / 1000.0),
status.outputBits,
)
status.fallbackReason != null -> stringResource(R.string.bit_perfect_status_unavailable, status.fallbackReason)
else -> stringResource(R.string.bit_perfect_status_waiting)
}

internal val GroupShape = RoundedCornerShape(14.dp)
internal val GROUP_INSET = 16.dp
internal val ROW_INSET = 16.dp
internal val ICON_SIZE = 22.dp
internal val ICON_GAP = 14.dp

/** Where a row's text starts — dividers are inset to match, as on iOS. */
internal val TEXT_INSET = ROW_INSET + ICON_SIZE + ICON_GAP

/**
* What is typed into the field under the Settings title, and whether anything
* on the screen has answered to it.
*
* A blank query matches everything, so the screen with the field untouched is
* the screen as it was before there was a field. Rows ask [matches] as they
* are composed; the empty state at the foot of the list reads [anyMatch] after
* every group has had its turn, which is why this is made fresh on each pass
* rather than remembered.
*/
private class SettingsSearch(
query: String,
/** Drawing one category's page rather than the main one: its top bar names it. */
val inPage: Boolean = false,
) {
// Trimmed, because a trailing space is a typo rather than a search for
// something ending in one — and on a phone keyboard it is one keystroke
// away from every word typed.
private val needle = query.trim()

var anyMatch = false
private set

fun matches(vararg keywords: String?): Boolean {
val hit = needle.isEmpty() ||
keywords.any { it?.contains(needle, ignoreCase = true) == true }
if (hit) anyMatch = true
return hit
}
}

/** Collects the rows of one group that survived the search. */
private class SettingsGroupScope(
private val search: SettingsSearch,
private val header: String?,
) {
class Entry(val divided: Boolean, val content: @Composable () -> Unit)

val entries = mutableListOf<Entry>()

/**
* One searchable setting. [keywords] is everything somebody might type
* looking for it: its title at least, plus whatever its subtitle or the
* controls under it say that the title doesn't — "Spotify", say, for the
* canvas link that lives under Animated cover art.
*
* [divided] is false for the rows drawn as part of the row above them
* rather than as settings in their own right, so they keep hugging their
* parent when both survive the filter.
*/
fun row(
vararg keywords: String?,
divided: Boolean = true,
content: @Composable () -> Unit,
) {
// The header counts for every row beneath it: searching "playback"
// should turn up the playback group entire, not nothing at all.
if (search.matches(header, *keywords)) entries += Entry(divided, content)
}
}

/**
* A [SettingsGroup] whose rows are filtered by the search field, and which
* takes itself off the screen when none of them are left. Dividers fall
* between the rows that survived rather than around the gaps left by the ones
* that didn't, so a filtered card is indistinguishable from a hand-written one.
*
* Inline so [content] is not a restartable lambda of its own. It only collects
* rows into [SettingsGroupScope.entries], and drawing them happens here: as its
* own recompose scope, a setting it reads — Automix hiding the crossfade
* slider, say — re-ran it alone, filling a list nothing redrew, and the row
* only came or went whenever something else recomposed the screen.
*/
@Composable
private inline fun SearchableSettingsGroup(
search: SettingsSearch,
header: String? = null,
footer: String? = null,
topSpacing: Dp = 26.dp,
content: @Composable SettingsGroupScope.() -> Unit,
) {
val scope = SettingsGroupScope(search, header)
scope.content()
if (scope.entries.isEmpty()) return
// A category's page is titled by its large heading; the header over its
// first card would only say the same word again. The card takes the
// header's place, straight under the heading, as on Account's page.
val inPageHeader = header != null && search.inPage
SettingsGroup(
header = header.takeUnless { inPageHeader },
footer = footer,
topSpacing = if (inPageHeader) 0.dp else topSpacing,
) {
scope.entries.forEachIndexed { index, entry ->
when {
index > 0 && entry.divided -> RowDivider()
// An undivided row is drawn tight to the top because something
// it belongs to is usually above it. Filtered down to itself it
// has nothing to sit under, so it is given that room back.
index == 0 && !entry.divided -> Spacer(Modifier.height(10.dp))
}
entry.content()
}
}
}

/**
* The large heading a Settings page leads with, under the bar's own small one —

*/

/**
* The standard row: glyph, title, optional subtitle, and on the right either
* [trailing] (a switch, say) or the current [value] followed by a chevron.
*
* [iconPainter] is for the handful of rows whose glyph is a drawable rather
* than a Material icon — the Dolby double-D, which is a mark and not something
* to approximate with the nearest speaker outline. Exactly one of it and [icon]
* is expected; the painter wins where both are given.
*/
@Composable
internal fun SettingsRow(
icon: ImageVector? = null,
title: String,
subtitle: String? = null,
subtitleContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
value: String? = null,
badge: String? = null,
enabled: Boolean = true,
iconPainter: Painter? = null,
onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null,
trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
) {
Row(
modifier = Modifier
.fillMaxWidth()
.then(if (onClick != null && enabled) Modifier.clickable(onClick = onClick) else Modifier)
.alpha(if (enabled) 1f else 0.45f)
.heightIn(min = 52.dp)
.padding(horizontal = ROW_INSET, vertical = 12.dp),
verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
) {
if (iconPainter != null) {
Icon(
painter = iconPainter,
contentDescription = null,
tint = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onBackground,
modifier = Modifier.size(ICON_SIZE),
)
} else if (icon != null) {
Icon(
imageVector = icon,
contentDescription = null,
tint = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onBackground,
modifier = Modifier.size(ICON_SIZE),
)
}
Spacer(Modifier.width(ICON_GAP))
Column(Modifier.weight(1f)) {
Row(verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
Text(
text = title,
style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge,
color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onBackground,
maxLines = 1,
overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
)
if (badge != null) {
Spacer(Modifier.width(8.dp))
Badge(badge)
}
}
if (subtitleContent != null) {
subtitleContent()
} else if (subtitle != null) {
Text(
text = subtitle,
style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
maxLines = 5,
)
}
}
Spacer(Modifier.width(12.dp))
if (trailing != null) {
trailing()
} else if (value != null || onClick != null) {
if (value != null) {
Text(
text = value,
style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge,
color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
maxLines = 1,
)
Spacer(Modifier.width(4.dp))
}
Chevron()
}
}
}

enum class SettingsCategory(@param:StringRes val title: Int) {

LOCAL_MUSIC(R.string.local_music),

MISCELLANEOUS(R.string.miscellaneous),

;

val icon: ImageVector
get() = when (this) {

PLAYBACK -> SfIcons.PlayCircle

/** The settings whose options are a page of their own — see [SettingsChoicePage]. */
enum class SettingsChoiceKind(@param:StringRes val title: Int) {
AUDIO_QUALITY_WIFI(R.string.on_wifi),
AUDIO_QUALITY_CELLULAR(R.string.on_mobile_data),
DOWNLOAD_QUALITY(R.string.download_quality),
AUTOMIX_PERFORMANCE(R.string.automix_performance),
BIT_PERFECT(R.string.bit_perfect_output),

}

/** The main page's list of categories: a glyph and a name each, and a chevron into it. */
@Composable
private fun SettingsCategoryList(onOpen: (SettingsCategory) -> Unit) {
SettingsGroup {
SettingsCategory.entries.forEachIndexed { index, category ->
if (index > 0) RowDivider()
SettingsRow(
icon = category.icon,
title = stringResource(category.title),
onClick = { onOpen(category) },
)
}
}
}

/**
* One of [SettingsChoiceKind]'s settings as a page: its options in a card,
* the one in force ticked, and what the choice is about in the footer. A pick
* is saved at once and [onChosen] then leaves the page, as the drawer this
* replaces closed on one.
*/
@Composable
fun SettingsChoicePage(
choice: SettingsChoiceKind,
onChosen: () -> Unit,
/** Asks before a bit-perfect mode is turned on — see [SettingsScreen]. */
onConfirmBitPerfect: (BitPerfectMode) -> Unit,
contentPadding: PaddingValues,
modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
Column(
modifier
.fillMaxWidth()
.verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())
.padding(contentPadding),
) {
SettingsPageTitle(stringResource(choice.title))
when (choice) {
SettingsChoiceKind.AUDIO_QUALITY_WIFI, SettingsChoiceKind.AUDIO_QUALITY_CELLULAR -> {
val wifi = choice == SettingsChoiceKind.AUDIO_QUALITY_WIFI
val wifiQuality by AppSettings.audioQualityWifi.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
val cellularQuality by AppSettings.audioQualityCellular.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
ChoiceGroup(
// Best first — the option most people want shouldn't be last.
options = AudioQuality.entries.reversed(),
selected = if (wifi) wifiQuality else cellularQuality,
label = { it.localizedLabel() },
detail = { stringResource(R.string.quality_hourly, it.detail, it.hourly) },
footer = stringResource(
R.string.audio_quality_connection,
stringResource(if (wifi) R.string.wifi else R.string.mobile_data).lowercase(Locale.getDefault()),
),
) { quality ->
// Writes the one ceiling being edited and nothing else —
// which sources a rung consults is read per stream off the
// connection in force; see [AudioQuality.permits].
if (wifi) AppSettings.setAudioQualityWifi(quality) else AppSettings.setAudioQualityCellular(quality)
onChosen()
}
}

// Priced per track rather than per hour, unlike the streaming
// ceilings: a stream is paid for again on every replay, a download
// once. Same list, different question.
SettingsChoiceKind.DOWNLOAD_QUALITY -> {
val selected by AppSettings.downloadQuality.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
ChoiceGroup(
options = DownloadQuality.entries.reversed(),
selected = selected,
label = { it.localizedLabel() },
detail = { stringResource(R.string.quality_per_track, it.detail, it.perTrack) },
footer = stringResource(R.string.download_quality_dialog_subtitle),
) { quality ->
AppSettings.setDownloadQuality(quality)
onChosen()
}
}

SettingsChoiceKind.AUTOMIX_PERFORMANCE -> {
val selected by AppSettings.automixPerformanceMode.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
ChoiceGroup(
options = AutomixPerformanceMode.entries,
selected = selected,
label = { it.localizedLabel() },
detail = {
stringResource(
when (it) {
AutomixPerformanceMode.EFFICIENT -> R.string.automix_mode_efficient_subtitle
AutomixPerformanceMode.BALANCED -> R.string.automix_mode_balanced_subtitle
AutomixPerformanceMode.PERFORMANCE -> R.string.automix_mode_performance_subtitle
},
)
},
footer = stringResource(R.string.automix_performance_warning),
) { mode ->
AppSettings.setAutomixPerformanceMode(mode)
onChosen()
}
}

SettingsChoiceKind.BIT_PERFECT -> {
val selected by AppSettings.bitPerfectMode.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
ChoiceGroup(
options = BitPerfectMode.entries,
selected = selected,
label = { it.localizedLabel() },
detail = { it.description() },
footer = stringResource(R.string.bit_perfect_sheet_warning),
enabled = { it.isSupported },
) { mode ->
onChosen()
// Leaving the mode needs no warning; entering it hands
// volume to the DAC, at full scale.
if (mode == BitPerfectMode.OFF) AppSettings.setBitPerfectMode(mode) else onConfirmBitPerfect(mode)
}
}

SettingsChoiceKind.ACCENT -> {
// No onChosen: the page stays up so the new accent can be seen
// taking hold behind the swatches before going back.
val selected by AppSettings.accentColor.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
AccentColorPicker(selected = selected, onSelect = AppSettings::setAccentColor)
}

SettingsChoiceKind.FONT -> {
val selected by AppSettings.appFont.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
ChoiceGroup(
options = AppFont.entries,
selected = selected,
label = { it.localizedLabel() },
detail = { it.description() },
footer = stringResource(R.string.font_footer),
) { font ->
AppSettings.setAppFont(font)
onChosen()
}
}
}
Spacer(Modifier.height(32.dp))
}
}

/** The accent colours as a grid of swatches, the one in force haloed and ticked. */
@Composable
private fun AccentColorPicker(
selected: AccentColor,
onSelect: (AccentColor) -> Unit,
) {
val haptics = LocalHapticFeedback.current
val isDark = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background.luminance() < 0.5f
SettingsGroup(footer = stringResource(R.string.accent_color_footer), topSpacing = 0.dp) {
Column(Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(vertical = 8.dp)) {
AccentColor.entries.chunked(5).forEach { line ->
Row(
modifier = Modifier
.fillMaxWidth()
.padding(horizontal = ROW_INSET, vertical = 8.dp),
horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
) {
line.forEach { accent ->
val tint = Color(if (isDark) accent.dark else accent.light)
Box(
modifier = Modifier
.size(52.dp)
.clip(CircleShape)
.background(
if (accent == selected) tint.copy(alpha = 0.25f) else Color.Transparent,
CircleShape,
)
.clickable {
haptics.performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackType.TextHandleMove)
onSelect(accent)
}
.padding(6.dp)
.background(tint, CircleShape),
contentAlignment = Alignment.Center,
) {
if (accent == selected) {
Icon(
imageVector = Icons.Rounded.Check,
contentDescription = accent.localizedLabel(),
tint = Color(accent.onAccent),
modifier = Modifier.size(24.dp),
)
}
}
}
repeat(5 - line.size) { Spacer(Modifier.size(52.dp)) }
}
}
}
}
}

/**
* A card of options, one of them ticked: the body of every choice page. A
* label and a dimmer line under it per option; [enabled] greys out the ones
* this device can't take.
*/
@Composable
internal fun <T> ChoiceGroup(
options: List<T>,
selected: T,
label: @Composable (T) -> String,
footer: String?,
detail: (@Composable (T) -> String)? = null,
enabled: (T) -> Boolean = { true },
onSelect: (T) -> Unit,
) {
val haptics = LocalHapticFeedback.current
// Every page it is the body of leads with its large heading — see
// [SettingsPageTitle], whose own bottom padding is all the room it needs.
SettingsGroup(footer = footer, topSpacing = 0.dp) {
options.forEachIndexed { index, option ->
if (index > 0) {
HorizontalDivider(
modifier = Modifier.padding(start = ROW_INSET),
thickness = 0.5.dp,
color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outline,
)
}
val available = enabled(option)
Row(
modifier = Modifier
.fillMaxWidth()
.clickable(enabled = available) {
haptics.performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackType.TextHandleMove)
onSelect(option)
}
.alpha(if (available) 1f else 0.45f)
.heightIn(min = 52.dp)
.padding(horizontal = ROW_INSET, vertical = 12.dp),
verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
) {
Column(Modifier.weight(1f)) {
Text(
text = label(option),
style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge,
color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onBackground,
)
detail?.let {
Text(
text = it(option),
style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
)
}
}
if (option == selected) {
Spacer(Modifier.width(12.dp))
Icon(
SfIcons.Check,
contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.selected),
tint = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary,
modifier = Modifier.size(20.dp),
)
}
}
}
}
}

@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)
@Composable
fun BitChordTheme(
    darkTheme: Boolean = isSystemInDarkTheme(),
    font: AppFont = AppFont.DEFAULT,
    accent: AccentColor = AccentColor.RED,
    content: @Composable () -> Unit,
) {
    val scheme = remember(darkTheme, accent) {
        (if (darkTheme) DarkColors else LightColors).withAccent(accent, darkTheme)
    }
    val selection = remember(scheme.primary) {
        TextSelectionColors(
            handleColor = scheme.primary,
            backgroundColor = scheme.primary.copy(alpha = 0.3f),
        )
    }
    MaterialTheme(
        colorScheme = scheme,
        typography = when (font) {
            AppFont.DEFAULT -> BitChordTypography
            AppFont.LEGACY -> LegacyTypography
        },
        shapes = AppleShapes,
    ) {
        // iOS draws no Material ripple. Null switches off the one the remaining
        // Material buttons and menu rows still carried; the app's own controls
        // already pass indication = null and keep their own press behaviour.
        CompositionLocalProvider(
            LocalRippleConfiguration provides null,
            LocalTextSelectionColors provides selection,
            content = content,
        )
    }
}

/**
 * Draws the status and navigation bar glyphs dark or light.
 *
 * `enableEdgeToEdge()` decides this from the *system* dark-mode setting, which
 * is the wrong input the moment the in-app theme disagrees with it: Light theme
 * on a phone in dark mode left white icons on a white bar, invisible. The bars
 * have to follow the content the app is actually painting. The player supplies
 * its own stable light-icon value and paints contrast behind it; every other
 * surface follows the theme. Hence a parameter rather than reading it here.
 */
@Composable
fun SystemBarIcons(dark: Boolean) {
    val view = LocalView.current
    if (view.isInEditMode) return
    val window = findWindow(view) ?: return
    SideEffect {
        WindowCompat.getInsetsController(window, view).apply {
            isAppearanceLightStatusBars = dark
            isAppearanceLightNavigationBars = dark
        }
    }
}

* nothing for semibold titles at 18 to 24. The large titles had nothing to
* measure against and follow the same trend.
*/
private val BitChordTypography = Typography(
displayLarge = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W800, fontSize = 34.sp, letterSpacing = (-0.5).sp),
headlineLarge = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W800, fontSize = 30.sp, letterSpacing = (-0.4).sp),
headlineMedium = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W700, fontSize = 22.sp, letterSpacing = (-0.25).sp),
titleLarge = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W700, fontSize = 20.sp, letterSpacing = (-0.2).sp),
titleMedium = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W600, fontSize = 16.sp, letterSpacing = 0.05.sp),
bodyLarge = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W400, fontSize = 16.sp, letterSpacing = 0.2.sp),
bodyMedium = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W400, fontSize = 14.sp, letterSpacing = 0.3.sp),
labelMedium = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W600, fontSize = 12.sp, letterSpacing = 0.25.sp),
labelSmall = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W600, fontSize = 11.sp, letterSpacing = 0.3.sp),
).withFamily(SFProDisplay)

/**
* SF Pro Display as the app first shipped it, before [SFProDisplay] moved every
* weight a cut lighter: each weight draws its own cut, Heavy included. Kept for
* [AppFont.LEGACY].
*/
val SFProDisplayLegacy = FontFamily(
Font(R.font.sf_pro_display_regular, FontWeight.W400),
Font(R.font.sf_pro_display_medium, FontWeight.W500),
Font(R.font.sf_pro_display_semibold, FontWeight.W600),
Font(R.font.sf_pro_display_bold, FontWeight.W700),
Font(R.font.sf_pro_display_heavy, FontWeight.W800),
)

// Heavy, tight typography — the original scale [AppFont.LEGACY] restores.
private val LegacyTypography = Typography(
displayLarge = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W800, fontSize = 34.sp, letterSpacing = (-0.8).sp),
headlineLarge = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W800, fontSize = 30.sp, letterSpacing = (-0.7).sp),
headlineMedium = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W700, fontSize = 22.sp, letterSpacing = (-0.4).sp),
titleLarge = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W700, fontSize = 20.sp, letterSpacing = (-0.3).sp),
titleMedium = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W600, fontSize = 16.sp, letterSpacing = (-0.2).sp),
bodyLarge = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W400, fontSize = 16.sp),
bodyMedium = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W400, fontSize = 14.sp),
labelMedium = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W600, fontSize = 12.sp),
labelSmall = TextStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.W600, fontSize = 11.sp),
).withFamily(SFProDisplayLegacy)

/** Applies [family] to every style in the scale, so nothing is left on Roboto. */
private fun Typography.withFamily(family: FontFamily) = Typography(
displayLarge = displayLarge.copy(fontFamily = family),
displayMedium = displayMedium.copy(fontFamily = family),
displaySmall = displaySmall.copy(fontFamily = family),
headlineLarge = headlineLarge.copy(fontFamily = family),
headlineMedium = headlineMedium.copy(fontFamily = family),
headlineSmall = headlineSmall.copy(fontFamily = family),
titleLarge = titleLarge.copy(fontFamily = family),
titleMedium = titleMedium.copy(fontFamily = family),
titleSmall = titleSmall.copy(fontFamily = family),
bodyLarge = bodyLarge.copy(fontFamily = family),
bodyMedium = bodyMedium.copy(fontFamily = family),
bodySmall = bodySmall.copy(fontFamily = family),
labelLarge = labelLarge.copy(fontFamily = family),
labelMedium = labelMedium.copy(fontFamily = family),
labelSmall = labelSmall.copy(fontFamily = family),
)

@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)
@Composable
fun BitChordTheme(
darkTheme: Boolean = isSystemInDarkTheme(),
font: AppFont = AppFont.DEFAULT,
accent: AccentColor = AccentColor.RED,
content: @Composable () -> Unit,
) {
val scheme = remember(darkTheme, accent) {
(if (darkTheme) DarkColors else LightColors).withAccent(accent, darkTheme)
}
val selection = remember(scheme.primary) {
TextSelectionColors(
handleColor = scheme.primary,
backgroundColor = scheme.primary.copy(alpha = 0.3f),
)
}
MaterialTheme(
colorScheme = scheme,
typography = when (font) {
AppFont.DEFAULT -> BitChordTypography
AppFont.LEGACY -> LegacyTypography
},
shapes = AppleShapes,
) {
// iOS draws no Material ripple. Null switches off the one the remaining
// Material buttons and menu rows still carried; the app's own controls
// already pass indication = null and keep their own press behaviour.
CompositionLocalProvider(
LocalRippleConfiguration provides null,
LocalTextSelectionColors provides selection,
content = content,
)
}
}

/**
* Draws the status and navigation bar glyphs dark or light.
*
* `enableEdgeToEdge()` decides this from the *system* dark-mode setting, which
* is the wrong input the moment the in-app theme disagrees with it: Light theme
* on a phone in dark mode left white icons on a white bar, invisible. The bars
* have to follow the content the app is actually painting. The player supplies
* its own stable light-icon value and paints contrast behind it; every other
* surface follows the theme. Hence a parameter rather than reading it here.
*/
@Composable
fun SystemBarIcons(dark: Boolean) {
val view = LocalView.current
if (view.isInEditMode) return
val window = findWindow(view) ?: return
SideEffect {
WindowCompat.getInsetsController(window, view).apply {
isAppearanceLightStatusBars = dark
isAppearanceLightNavigationBars = dark
}
}
}

package com.music.bitchord.widget

import android.content.Context

/**
 * Everything a home-screen widget needs to know about playback.
 *
 * Persisted rather than read live, because a widget outlives the app. It is on
 * screen while the process is dead, after a reboot, and in the seconds before a
 * launcher's first update reaches us — none of which a
 * [MediaController][androidx.media3.session.MediaController] can serve, since
 * connecting one means starting [PlaybackService][com.music.bitchord.playback.PlaybackService]
 * just to find out what to draw. So the service writes here whenever the answer
 * changes ([publishWidgetState][com.music.bitchord.playback.PlaybackService]) and
 * the widget only ever reads a file.
 */
internal data class MediaWidgetSnapshot(
    val mediaId: String?,
    val title: String,
    val artist: String,
    val artworkUrl: String?,
    /**
     * Whether the transport should show a pause glyph.
     *
     * This tracks `player.playWhenReady`, **not** `player.isPlaying`. The
     * difference matters more here than almost anywhere else in the app: a
     * YouTube track has to be resolved through NewPipe before it can buffer, and
     * that can run for seconds, all of which `isPlaying` spends false. Keyed on
     * it, a widget would answer a tap by leaving the play glyph exactly where it
     * was — the one thing that makes a control feel broken. `playWhenReady`
     * flips the instant the command lands, which is also what the media
     * notification shows.
     */
    val isPlaying: Boolean,
    val hasPrevious: Boolean,
    val hasNext: Boolean,
    /** Whether the track is liked. Drawn by the 4×1 widget's star. */
    val isLiked: Boolean = false,
    /**
     * Whether Like is offered for this track at all — the player's own rule:
     * signed in, and not a local file or a download. The star is hidden, not
     * disabled, when it is false, as it is in the player.
     */
    val canLike: Boolean = false,
    /** Whether shuffle is on. Drawn by the 4×1 widget's Shuffle. */
    val shuffleEnabled: Boolean = false,
) {
    /** Whether there is a track to draw at all. */
    val hasTrack: Boolean get() = mediaId != null

    companion object {

        val EMPTY = MediaWidgetSnapshot(
            mediaId = null,
            title = "",
            artist = "",
            artworkUrl = null,
            isPlaying = false,
            hasPrevious = false,
            hasNext = false,
        )

        fun save(context: Context, snapshot: MediaWidgetSnapshot) {
            prefs(context).edit()
                .putString(KEY_MEDIA_ID, snapshot.mediaId)
                .putString(KEY_TITLE, snapshot.title)
                .putString(KEY_ARTIST, snapshot.artist)
                .putString(KEY_ARTWORK, snapshot.artworkUrl)
                .putBoolean(KEY_PLAYING, snapshot.isPlaying)
                .putBoolean(KEY_HAS_PREVIOUS, snapshot.hasPrevious)
                .putBoolean(KEY_HAS_NEXT, snapshot.hasNext)
                .putBoolean(KEY_LIKED, snapshot.isLiked)
                .putBoolean(KEY_CAN_LIKE, snapshot.canLike)
                .putBoolean(KEY_SHUFFLE, snapshot.shuffleEnabled)
                .apply()
        }

        /** The last state published by the live playback service. */
        fun load(context: Context): MediaWidgetSnapshot {
            val prefs = prefs(context)
            val mediaId = prefs.getString(KEY_MEDIA_ID, null)
            if (mediaId != null) {
                return MediaWidgetSnapshot(
                    mediaId = mediaId,
                    title = prefs.getString(KEY_TITLE, "").orEmpty(),
                    artist = prefs.getString(KEY_ARTIST, "").orEmpty(),
                    artworkUrl = prefs.getString(KEY_ARTWORK, null),
                    isPlaying = prefs.getBoolean(KEY_PLAYING, false),
                    hasPrevious = prefs.getBoolean(KEY_HAS_PREVIOUS, false),
                    hasNext = prefs.getBoolean(KEY_HAS_NEXT, false),
                    isLiked = prefs.getBoolean(KEY_LIKED, false),
                    canLike = prefs.getBoolean(KEY_CAN_LIKE, false),
                    shuffleEnabled = prefs.getBoolean(KEY_SHUFFLE, false),
                )
            }
            return EMPTY
        }

        private fun prefs(context: Context) =
            context.getSharedPreferences("bitchord_widget", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)

        private const val KEY_MEDIA_ID = "media_id"
        private const val KEY_TITLE = "title"
        private const val KEY_ARTIST = "artist"
        private const val KEY_ARTWORK = "artwork"
        private const val KEY_PLAYING = "playing"
        private const val KEY_HAS_PREVIOUS = "has_previous"
        private const val KEY_HAS_NEXT = "has_next"
        private const val KEY_LIKED = "liked"
        private const val KEY_CAN_LIKE = "can_like"
        private const val KEY_SHUFFLE = "shuffle"
    }
}

app/src/main/res/drawable/ic_widget_play.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  Play. Rounded rather than sharp, to sit alongside the Icons.Rounded glyphs the
  mini player and the full player use.

  The rounding is a round-joined stroke of the fill's own colour laid over an
  inset triangle, rather than arcs written by hand: the stroke extends half its
  width past the path and caps every corner with a radius of exactly that half,
  so insetting the triangle by the same amount lands the finished glyph back on
  the bounds Material's own play_arrow occupies. Hand-authored arcs would give
  the same picture with three more chances to get a control point wrong.

  White, not tinted: this only ever draws over darkened album art, so there is
  no theme for it to follow.
-->
<vector xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:width="24dp"
    android:height="24dp"
    android:viewportWidth="24"
    android:viewportHeight="24">
    <path
        android:fillColor="#FFFFFFFF"
        android:pathData="M8.4,6.4L8.4,17.6L17.6,12Z"
        android:strokeColor="#FFFFFFFF"
        android:strokeLineCap="round"
        android:strokeLineJoin="round"
        android:strokeWidth="2.6" />
</vector>

app/src/main/res/drawable/widget_pill_ba.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  The 4×1 widget's body: a dark translucent capsule over the wallpaper. A
  RemoteViews can't blur what is behind it, so it is tinted instead — dark
  enough that white text holds on a light wallpaper, light enough that the
  wallpaper still shows through. The radius is simply larger than the pill is
  ever tall, which clamps to a full capsule at any height.
-->
<shape xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:shape="rectangle">
    <corners android:radius="200dp" />
    <solid android:color="#A6141619" />
</shape>

<!--
  Stand-in artwork. Used two ways, and it has to work as both: as the picker
  preview's cover, where no real track exists yet, and as what the widget draws
  when a track genuinely has no artwork.

  Only the top two stops are the "cover"; the bottom third darkens on its own,
  standing in for the scrim the compositor bakes over real artwork so the
  transport is legible over this too.
-->
<shape xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:shape="rectangle">
    <corners android:radius="@dimen/widget_corner_radius" />
    <gradient
        android:angle="270"
        android:centerColor="#FF1B2130"
        android:centerY="0.45"
        android:endColor="#FF07090E"
        android:startColor="#FF2E3446"
        android:type="linear" />
</shape>

app/src/main/res/layout/widget_media_com.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  The 2×2 widget, and the shape either widget takes when it is narrower than
  MediaWidget.WIDE_LAYOUT_MIN_DP: full-bleed artwork with the track name over
  three centred transport buttons, in a band at the foot of it.

  Stacked rather than set beside the buttons like widget_media_wide does it. Two
  cells is 110dp, of which the transport alone wants 40; a title sharing that
  line would have some 20dp left and show two or three characters, so it takes a
  line of its own and the band grows to fit. No artist: one line of text is what
  a square this size can carry legibly, and the song is the half of it worth
  having.

  The band is the *only* thing laid over the artwork; the blur that makes it
  readable is baked into the bitmap widget_art shows, because RemoteViews has no
  way to blur anything at runtime. Its height therefore has to match the region
  MediaWidgetArt blurred, which is why both read @dimen/widget_band_compact.

  The band is deliberately not clickable, so a tap on its empty space falls
  through to widget_art beneath and opens the app, like a tap anywhere else on
  the cover.
-->
<FrameLayout xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:id="@+id/widget_root"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="match_parent"
    android:background="@drawable/widget_preview_art">

    <!--
      fitXY, not centerCrop: the bitmap is composited at the widget's exact pixel
      size with the cover already centre-cropped into it, so this is a 1:1 blit.
      Asking for centerCrop here would crop a second time, and the blurred band —
      which is pinned to the bitmap's bottom edge — would be the first thing to
      be cropped off.
    -->
    <ImageView
        android:id="@+id/widget_art"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="match_parent"
        android:contentDescription="@string/widget_artwork"
        android:scaleType="fitXY" />

    <LinearLayout
        android:id="@+id/widget_band"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_band_compact"
        android:layout_gravity="bottom"
        android:gravity="center_horizontal|bottom"
        android:orientation="vertical"
        android:paddingLeft="@dimen/widget_band_padding"
        android:paddingRight="@dimen/widget_band_padding"
        android:paddingBottom="4dp">

        <!--
          Centred, and padded in past the band's own inset: at this width a title
          runs to the ellipsis more often than not, and one that ended flush with
          the widget's edge would read as clipped rather than as shortened.
        -->
        <TextView
            android:id="@+id/widget_title"
            android:layout_width="match_parent"
            android:layout_height="wrap_content"
            android:layout_marginBottom="3dp"
            android:ellipsize="end"
            android:fontFamily="@font/sf_pro_display_semibold"
            android:gravity="center_horizontal"
            android:includeFontPadding="false"
            android:maxLines="1"
            android:paddingLeft="4dp"
            android:paddingRight="4dp"
            android:textColor="#FFFFFFFF"
            android:textSize="13sp" />

        <!--
          Weighted rather than three fixed 40dp buttons centred: at two cells the
          band has 94dp of content width and three of those want 120, so a fixed
          row overflows and the launcher clips the last glyph off. Sharing the
          width out instead means the buttons spread as the widget grows and
          close up as it shrinks, and the glyphs — which are padded in, not sized
          by the box — hold 22dp until there is genuinely no room.
        -->
        <LinearLayout
            android:layout_width="match_parent"
            android:layout_height="wrap_content"
            android:orientation="horizontal">

            <ImageView
                android:id="@+id/widget_previous"
                android:layout_width="0dp"
                android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_button_compact"
                android:layout_weight="1"
                android:background="@drawable/widget_transport_button"
                android:contentDescription="@string/widget_previous"
                android:padding="9dp"
                android:src="@drawable/ic_widget_previous" />

            <ImageView
                android:id="@+id/widget_toggle"
                android:layout_width="0dp"
                android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_button_compact"
                android:layout_weight="1"
                android:background="@drawable/widget_transport_button"
                android:contentDescription="@string/widget_play"
                android:padding="9dp"
                android:src="@drawable/ic_widget_play" />

            <ImageView
                android:id="@+id/widget_next"
                android:layout_width="0dp"
                android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_button_compact"
                android:layout_weight="1"
                android:background="@drawable/widget_transport_button"
                android:contentDescription="@string/widget_next"
                android:padding="9dp"
                android:src="@drawable/ic_widget_next" />
        </LinearLayout>
    </LinearLayout>
</FrameLayout>

        android:layout_gravity="bottom"

        android:orientation="vertical"

            android:layout_width="match_parent"
            android:layout_height="wrap_content"
            android:layout_marginBottom="3dp"
            android:ellipsize="end"
            android:fontFamily="@font/sf_pro_display_semibold"
            android:gravity="center_horizontal"
            android:includeFontPadding="false"

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  The 4×1 widget: a capsule with the cover in a circle at its left, and the
  track over Like, previous, play, next and Shuffle beside it.

  The capsule is wrap_content and centred rather than filling the cell. A
  one-row cell is anywhere from ~60dp to over 100dp tall depending on the
  launcher, and a capsule stretched to the taller end stops reading as one.
  Its height is the cover plus an even 7dp all round, so the text column is
  sized to fit inside the cover's 64dp: a 19dp title over a 38dp button row.

  The title sits directly on the button row, with no gap: the glyphs are
  padded inside their 38dp squares, so the air between the two lines comes
  from the buttons themselves, and any margin on top made the capsule look
  loose below the buttons and tight above the title.
  The column's 4dp top margin evens out the ink: each glyph leaves ~11dp of
  its button empty below it, the title's ink starts ~3dp into its line, so a
  column centred by its boxes sat high. In a centre_vertical LinearLayout a
  margin moves the child by its full amount, not half.

  The body is the cover itself, blurred to colour and darkened a little, the way
  the player's lyrics and queue stand on it. RemoteViews can't blur, so it is a
  bitmap MediaWidgetArt.pill bakes at the capsule's exact size; widget_pill_bg
  shows it. Until it arrives, the translucent capsule stands in.

  The buttons are fixed squares spread by equal spacers, not weighted cells.
  Weighted, each button was a fifth of the row wide — the ripple became an oval,
  the first glyph sat well in from where the title starts and the last well in
  from the capsule's edge. As squares the row runs flush from the title's left
  edge to the capsule's right padding.
  The spacers are empty FrameLayouts because a RemoteViews refuses to inflate
  a plain View — the launcher shows "Couldn't add widget" instead.

  Each glyph gets its own padding because the drawables don't share an optical
  size: the star and shuffle fill most of their 24-unit box, the transport
  glyphs barely half of it. Equal padding made the star look large and
  previous/next look small; these numbers make them read as one set.

  The root is transparent and not clickable, so a tap beside the capsule falls
  through to the home screen; widget_pill is what opens the app.
-->
<FrameLayout xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="match_parent">

    <FrameLayout
        android:id="@+id/widget_pill"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_pill_height"
        android:layout_gravity="center_vertical">

        <ImageView
            android:id="@+id/widget_pill_bg"
            android:layout_width="match_parent"
            android:layout_height="match_parent"
            android:background="@drawable/widget_pill_background"
            android:importantForAccessibility="no"
            android:scaleType="fitXY" />

        <LinearLayout
            android:layout_width="match_parent"
            android:layout_height="match_parent"
            android:gravity="center_vertical"
            android:orientation="horizontal"
            android:paddingLeft="7dp"
            android:paddingRight="12dp">

            <!--
              The bitmap arrives already cut to a circle — see MediaWidgetPill. The
              oval background is only what shows before it does.
            -->
            <ImageView
                android:id="@+id/widget_art"
                android:layout_width="@dimen/widget_pill_art"
                android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_pill_art"
                android:background="@drawable/widget_pill_art_placeholder"
                android:contentDescription="@string/widget_artwork"
                android:scaleType="fitXY" />

            <LinearLayout
                android:layout_width="0dp"
                android:layout_height="wrap_content"
                android:layout_marginLeft="6dp"
                android:layout_marginTop="4dp"
                android:layout_weight="1"
                android:orientation="vertical">

                <!--
                  Inset by the star's own inset inside its button (9dp of padding
                  plus the glyph's side bearing), so the text starts exactly above
                  the star rather than to the left of it.
                -->
                <TextView
                    android:id="@+id/widget_title"
                    android:layout_width="match_parent"
                    android:layout_height="wrap_content"
                    android:ellipsize="end"
                    android:fontFamily="@font/sf_pro_display_semibold"
                    android:includeFontPadding="false"
                    android:maxLines="1"
                    android:paddingLeft="10dp"
                    android:paddingRight="10dp"
                    android:textColor="#FFFFFFFF"
                    android:textSize="16sp" />

                <LinearLayout
                    android:layout_width="match_parent"
                    android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_button_pill"
                    android:gravity="center_vertical"
                    android:orientation="horizontal">

                    <ImageView
                        android:id="@+id/widget_like"
                        android:layout_width="@dimen/widget_button_pill"
                        android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_button_pill"
                        android:background="@drawable/widget_transport_button"
                        android:contentDescription="@string/like"
                        android:padding="9dp"
                        android:src="@drawable/ic_widget_star" />

                    <FrameLayout
                        android:layout_width="0dp"
                        android:layout_height="1dp"
                        android:layout_weight="1" />

                    <ImageView
                        android:id="@+id/widget_previous"
                        android:layout_width="@dimen/widget_button_pill"
                        android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_button_pill"
                        android:background="@drawable/widget_transport_button"
                        android:contentDescription="@string/widget_previous"
                        android:padding="6dp"
                        android:src="@drawable/ic_widget_previous" />

                    <FrameLayout
                        android:layout_width="0dp"
                        android:layout_height="1dp"
                        android:layout_weight="1" />

                    <ImageView
                        android:id="@+id/widget_toggle"
                        android:layout_width="@dimen/widget_button_pill"
                        android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_button_pill"
                        android:background="@drawable/widget_transport_button"
                        android:contentDescription="@string/widget_play"
                        android:padding="4dp"
                        android:src="@drawable/ic_widget_play" />

                    <FrameLayout
                        android:layout_width="0dp"
                        android:layout_height="1dp"
                        android:layout_weight="1" />

                    <ImageView
                        android:id="@+id/widget_next"
                        android:layout_width="@dimen/widget_button_pill"
                        android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_button_pill"
                        android:background="@drawable/widget_transport_button"
                        android:contentDescription="@string/widget_next"
                        android:padding="6dp"
                        android:src="@drawable/ic_widget_next" />

                    <FrameLayout
                        android:layout_width="0dp"
                        android:layout_height="1dp"
                        android:layout_weight="1" />

                    <ImageView
                        android:id="@+id/widget_shuffle"
                        android:layout_width="@dimen/widget_button_pill"
                        android:layout_height="@dimen/widget_button_pill"
                        android:background="@drawable/widget_transport_button"
                        android:contentDescription="@string/shuffle_off"
                        android:padding="8dp"
                        android:src="@drawable/ic_widget_shuffle" />
                </LinearLayout>
            </LinearLayout>
        </LinearLayout>
    </FrameLayout>
</FrameLayout>

<!--

  MediaWidget.WIDE_LAYOUT_MIN_DP or wider. Same full-bleed cover and same baked
  blur as widget_media_compact; the extra width goes to the track, because three
  glyphs spread across four cells reads as an empty bar.

  See widget_media_compact for why the band's height has to match the blurred
  region, and why nothing in it is clickable except the buttons themselves.
-->
<FrameLayout xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:id="@+id/widget_root"

<string name="addon_blocked_quality">Die Audioqualität über %1$s ist auf %2$s eingestellt. Songs von %3$s werden nur in Verlustfrei abgespielt – ändere das unter Einstellungen → Audioqualität, um diesen abzuspielen.</string>
<string name="addon_blocked_watch">Die Musik läuft über deine Uhr, die den Ton unter Verlustfrei begrenzt. Songs von %1$s spielen wieder, sobald dein Telefon die Musik zurückholt.</string>
<string name="download_addon_left_out_title">Download ohne %1$s</string>
<string name="download_addon_not_allowed">%1$s erlaubt keine Downloads, deshalb werden deine Songs aus deinen anderen Quellen gespeichert.</string>
<string name="download_addon_needs_lossless_output">%1$s liefert Musik nur, solange kabelgebundene, USB- oder LDAC-Kopfhörer verbunden sind. Downloads überspringen es, bis welche verbunden sind, deshalb werden deine Songs aus deinen anderen Quellen gespeichert.</string>

<string name="font_legacy_subtitle">SF Pro Display · Ursprüngliche kräftige Schriftschnitte</string>
<string name="font_footer">„Klassisch“ bringt die kräftigere, engere Schrift zurück, die die App verwendete, bevor sie an Apple Music angepasst wurde.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_output">Bit-perfekte Ausgabe</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_bypassed_footer">Die bit-perfekte Ausgabe ist bereit, daher werden die ausgegrauten Einstellungen umgangen und keine Dolby-Atmos-Versionen angefordert. Sie funktionieren wieder, wenn der DAC getrennt oder der Modus ausgeschaltet wird.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_sheet_warning">Sendet den Titel unverändert an den DAC. Equalizer, Lautstärkenormalisierung, Überblendung, Automix, Wiedergabegeschwindigkeit und die Lautstärke von BitChord werden umgangen.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_off_subtitle">Der Ton läuft über den Android-Mixer und die Effekte von BitChord.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_android">USB-DAC</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_android_subtitle">Android 14 öffnet den DAC mit der Abtastrate und Bittiefe des jeweiligen Titels, ohne Mischen oder Resampling.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_requires_android_14">Erfordert Android 14 oder neuer</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_dap_exclusive">Integrierter DAC (AAudio exklusiv)</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_dap_exclusive_subtitle">Für Musikplayer mit eigenem DAC. Öffnet den Kopfhörer- oder Line-Ausgang exklusiv mit der Abtastrate des jeweiligen Titels. Nicht jedes Gerät gewährt den Exklusivmodus.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_requires_android_8_1">Erfordert Android 8.1 oder neuer</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_direct">USB-DAC (direkter Treiber)</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_direct_subtitle">BitChord steuert den DAC selbst, unter jeder Android-Version, und stellt die Lautstärke am DAC ein. Fragt nach der USB-Berechtigung. Kann deutlich lauter sein als die normale Ausgabe.</string>
<string name="dac_volume">DAC-Lautstärke</string>
<string name="dac_volume_subtitle">Wird am DAC selbst eingestellt; die Musik wird nicht skaliert</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume">DACs ohne Lautstärkeregelung zulassen</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_subtitle">Sonst spielt ein solcher DAC über die normale Ausgabe</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_confirm_title">Mit voller Aussteuerung abspielen?</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_confirm_message">BitChord kann die Lautstärke dieser Art von DAC nicht einstellen. Er spielt daher mit voller Aussteuerung, und nur sein eigener Regler, falls vorhanden, ändert die Lautstärke. Mit empfindlichen Kopfhörern kann das gefährlich laut sein.</string>
<string name="convert_for_limited_dac">Für einfachere DACs umwandeln</string>
<string name="convert_for_limited_dac_subtitle">Wandelt Titel, die über dem Limit deines DACs liegen, in sein höchstes Format um. Titel starten eventuell langsamer und sind nicht bit-perfekt zum Original.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_confirm_title">Bit-perfekte Ausgabe einschalten?</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_confirm_message">Der DAC erhält die Musik mit voller Aussteuerung, und die Lautstärketasten des Telefons funktionieren möglicherweise nicht mehr. Dreh den DAC oder Verstärker vor der Wiedergabe herunter.</string>

<string name="convert_for_limited_dac">Convertir para DAC más limitados</string>
<string name="convert_for_limited_dac_subtitle">Convierte las pistas que superan el límite de tu DAC a su formato más alto. Pueden tardar más en empezar y no serán bit-perfect respecto al original.</string>

<string name="font_footer">האפשרות קלאסי מחזירה את הגופן העבה והצפוף יותר שהאפליקציה השתמשה בו לפני שהותאמה ל-Apple Music.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_output">פלט Bit-perfect</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_bypassed_footer">פלט Bit-perfect מוכן, ולכן ההגדרות המעומעמות אינן פעילות ולא מתבקשות גרסאות Dolby Atmos. הן יפעלו שוב כשה-DAC ינותק או כשהמצב ייכבה.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_sheet_warning">שולח את הרצועה ל-DAC ללא שינוי. האקולייזר, נרמול העוצמה, ה-Crossfade, ה-Automix, מהירות ההשמעה ועוצמת הקול של BitChord אינם פעילים.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_off_subtitle">השמע עובר דרך המיקסר של Android והאפקטים של BitChord.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_android">USB DAC</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_android_subtitle">Android 14 פותח את ה-DAC בקצב ובעומק הסיביות של כל רצועה, ללא מיקס וללא דגימה מחדש.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_requires_android_14">נדרש Android 14 ומעלה</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_dap_exclusive">DAC מובנה (AAudio בלעדי)</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_dap_exclusive_subtitle">לנגני מוזיקה עם DAC משלהם. פותח את יציאת האוזניות או הקו באופן בלעדי בקצב של כל רצועה. לא כל מכשיר מאפשר מצב בלעדי.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_requires_android_8_1">נדרש Android 8.1 ומעלה</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_direct">USB DAC (מנהל התקן ישיר)</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_direct_subtitle">BitChord מפעיל את ה-DAC בעצמו, בכל גרסת Android, וקובע את עוצמת הקול ב-DAC. מבקש הרשאת USB. עשוי להישמע חזק בהרבה מהפלט הרגיל.</string>
<string name="dac_volume">עוצמת קול של ה-DAC</string>
<string name="dac_volume_subtitle">נקבעת ב-DAC עצמו; המוזיקה אינה משתנה</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume">אפשר רכיבי DAC ללא בקרת עוצמה</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_subtitle">אחרת, DAC כזה ינגן דרך הפלט הרגיל</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_confirm_title">לנגן בעוצמה מלאה?</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_confirm_message">BitChord לא יכול לקבוע את עוצמת הקול של DAC מסוג זה, ולכן הוא מנגן בעוצמה מלאה ורק הכפתור שלו עצמו, אם יש כזה, שולט בעוצמה. הצליל עלול להיות חזק באופן מסוכן עם אוזניות רגישות.</string>
<string name="convert_for_limited_dac">המרה לרכיבי DAC מוגבלים</string>
<string name="convert_for_limited_dac_subtitle">ממיר רצועות שמעל למגבלת ה-DAC שלך לפורמט הגבוה ביותר שלו. ייתכן שהרצועות יתחילו לאט יותר, והן לא יהיו Bit-perfect ביחס למקור.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_confirm_title">להפעיל פלט Bit-perfect?</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_confirm_message">ה-DAC מקבל את המוזיקה בעוצמה מלאה, וייתכן שכפתורי עוצמת הקול של הטלפון יפסיקו לעבוד. יש להנמיך את ה-DAC או המגבר לפני ההשמעה.</string>

<string name="bit_perfect_mode_dap_exclusive">बिल्ट-इन DAC (AAudio एक्सक्लूसिव)</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_dap_exclusive_subtitle">अपने DAC वाले म्यूज़िक प्लेयर के लिए। हर ट्रैक के अपने रेट पर हेडफ़ोन या लाइन आउटपुट को एक्सक्लूसिव रूप से खोलता है। हर डिवाइस एक्सक्लूसिव मोड नहीं देता।</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_requires_android_8_1">Android 8.1 या उसके बाद का वर्शन चाहिए</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_direct">USB DAC (डायरेक्ट ड्राइवर)</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_direct_subtitle">BitChord किसी भी Android वर्शन पर DAC को खुद चलाता है और वॉल्यूम DAC पर ही सेट करता है। USB अनुमति माँगता है। सामान्य आउटपुट से काफ़ी तेज़ हो सकता है।</string>
<string name="dac_volume">DAC वॉल्यूम</string>
<string name="dac_volume_subtitle">DAC पर ही सेट होता है; म्यूज़िक को स्केल नहीं किया जाता</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume">बिना वॉल्यूम कंट्रोल वाले DAC की अनुमति दें</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_subtitle">वरना ऐसा DAC सामान्य आउटपुट से चलेगा</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_confirm_title">फ़ुल स्केल पर चलाएँ?</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_confirm_message">BitChord इस तरह के DAC का वॉल्यूम सेट नहीं कर सकता, इसलिए यह फ़ुल स्केल पर चलता है और सिर्फ़ DAC का अपना नॉब, अगर हो, आवाज़ नियंत्रित करता है। संवेदनशील हेडफ़ोन पर यह ख़तरनाक रूप से तेज़ हो सकता है।</string>
<string name="convert_for_limited_dac">कम क्षमता वाले DAC के लिए बदलें</string>
<string name="convert_for_limited_dac_subtitle">आपके DAC की सीमा से ऊपर के ट्रैक को उसके सबसे ऊँचे फ़ॉर्मैट में बदलता है। ट्रैक शुरू होने में ज़्यादा समय लग सकता है और वे मूल के मुकाबले बिट-परफ़ेक्ट नहीं होंगे।</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_confirm_title">बिट-परफ़ेक्ट आउटपुट चालू करें?</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_confirm_message">DAC को म्यूज़िक फ़ुल स्केल पर मिलता है, और फ़ोन के वॉल्यूम बटन काम करना बंद कर सकते हैं। चलाने से पहले DAC या एम्पलीफ़ायर की आवाज़ कम कर लें।</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_status_active">%1$s · %2$s kHz · %3$d-बिट</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_status_dac_limited">%1$s · %2$s kHz · %3$d-बिट · DAC की अधिकतम सीमा, इस ट्रैक के फ़ॉर्मैट से बदला गया</string>

<string name="bit_perfect_output">Wyjście bit-perfect</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_bypassed_footer">Wyjście bit-perfect jest gotowe, więc wyszarzone ustawienia są pomijane, a wersje Dolby Atmos nie są pobierane. Zadziałają ponownie po odłączeniu DAC lub wyłączeniu trybu.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_sheet_warning">Wysyła utwór do DAC bez zmian. Equalizer, normalizacja głośności, crossfade, Automix, szybkość odtwarzania i głośność BitChord są pomijane.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_off_subtitle">Dźwięk przechodzi przez mikser Androida i efekty BitChord.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_android">DAC USB</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_android_subtitle">Android 14 otwiera DAC z częstotliwością i głębią bitową każdego utworu, bez miksowania i resamplingu.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_requires_android_14">Wymaga Androida 14 lub nowszego</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_dap_exclusive">Wbudowany DAC (AAudio na wyłączność)</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_dap_exclusive_subtitle">Do odtwarzaczy muzyki z własnym DAC. Otwiera wyjście słuchawkowe lub liniowe na wyłączność z częstotliwością każdego utworu. Nie każde urządzenie udostępnia tryb wyłączny.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_requires_android_8_1">Wymaga Androida 8.1 lub nowszego</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_direct">DAC USB (sterownik bezpośredni)</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_mode_usb_direct_subtitle">BitChord sam obsługuje DAC, w każdej wersji Androida, i ustawia głośność na DAC. Prosi o uprawnienia USB. Może grać znacznie głośniej niż zwykłe wyjście.</string>
<string name="dac_volume">Głośność DAC</string>
<string name="dac_volume_subtitle">Ustawiana na samym DAC; muzyka nie jest skalowana</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume">Zezwalaj na DAC bez regulacji głośności</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_subtitle">W przeciwnym razie taki DAC gra przez zwykłe wyjście</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_confirm_title">Odtwarzać w pełnej skali?</string>
<string name="usb_allow_fixed_volume_confirm_message">BitChord nie może ustawić głośności tego typu DAC, więc gra on w pełnej skali, a głośność reguluje tylko jego własne pokrętło, jeśli je ma. Na czułych słuchawkach może to być niebezpiecznie głośne.</string>
<string name="convert_for_limited_dac">Konwertuj dla słabszych DAC</string>
<string name="convert_for_limited_dac_subtitle">Konwertuje utwory powyżej limitu Twojego DAC do jego najwyższego formatu. Utwory mogą uruchamiać się dłużej i nie będą bit-perfect względem oryginału.</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_confirm_title">Włączyć wyjście bit-perfect?</string>
<string name="bit_perfect_confirm_message">DAC otrzymuje muzykę w pełnej skali, a przyciski głośności telefonu mogą przestać działać. Przed odtwarzaniem ścisz DAC lub wzmacniacz.</string>

<string name="bit_perfect_status_dac_limited">%1$s · %2$s kHz · %3$d bitów · maksimum DAC, przekonwertowano z formatu tego utworu</string>

<string name="bit_perfect_status_unavailable">Niedostępne dla tego utworu (%1$s)</string>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<resources>
    <!--
      From API 31 the launcher rounds every widget to this radius itself. Baking
      the same number into the artwork bitmap makes the two coincide; any other
      value shows up as either a square corner poking out of the host's mask or
      a transparent notch inside it.
    -->
    <dimen name="widget_corner_radius">@android:dimen/system_app_widget_background_radius</dimen>
</resources>

app/src/main/res/values/dimens.xml.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<resources>
    <!--
      The radius the launcher itself rounds a widget to. Overridden on API 31+
      with the platform's own value (values-v31), so the corners baked into the
      artwork bitmap land exactly where the host's clip does instead of leaving
      a sliver of square image outside a rounder mask. 16dp is the pre-31
      stand-in, where hosts don't clip at all and the baked corners are the only
      ones there are.
    -->
    <dimen name="widget_corner_radius">16dp</dimen>

    <!--
      The strip at the foot of the widget the track and transport sit in, and so
      exactly how much of the artwork the blur has to cover. Read by both the
      layout and the compositor — see MediaWidgetArt — because the two have to
      agree: a band taller than the blur puts buttons on sharp artwork, and a
      blur taller than the band puts a smudge above them with nothing on it.

      The compact one is the taller of the two despite being the smaller widget:
      it stacks the title over the buttons, where the wide one has the room to
      set them side by side.
    -->
    <dimen name="widget_band_compact">66dp</dimen>
    <dimen name="widget_band_wide">60dp</dimen>

    <!-- Inset of the transport from the widget's edges. -->
    <dimen name="widget_band_padding">8dp</dimen>

    <!-- Touch target and glyph size for one transport button. -->
    <dimen name="widget_button_compact">40dp</dimen>
    <dimen name="widget_button_wide">44dp</dimen>
    <dimen name="widget_glyph_compact">22dp</dimen>
    <dimen name="widget_glyph_wide">24dp</dimen>

    <!-- The 4×1 capsule: its height, round cover, and its row of five buttons. -->
    <dimen name="widget_pill_height">78dp</dimen>
    <dimen name="widget_pill_art">64dp</dimen>
    <dimen name="widget_button_pill">38dp</dimen>
</resources>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
   Auto-backup rules for Android 11 and older; data_extraction_rules.xml
   replaces these from Android 12.

   The encrypted stores are excluded because their keysets are wrapped by an
   Android Keystore key that never leaves the device: restored anywhere, they
   can't be decrypted (see EncryptedPrefs). Their plain fallbacks are excluded
   because they hold the same credentials in cleartext.
-->
<full-backup-content>
    <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="bitchord_auth.xml" />
    <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="bitchord_auth_plain.xml" />
    <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="bitchord_sources.xml" />
    <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="bitchord_sources_plain.xml" />
    <!-- Playback queues are local session state; do not resurrect them after reinstall. -->
    <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="bitchord_last_played.xml" />
    <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="bitchord_bounded_context.xml" />
    <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="bitchord_party_queue_stash.xml" />
</full-backup-content>

app/src/main/res/xml/file_paths.xml.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  What the FileProvider is allowed to hand out, which is these folders and no
  more.

  The Replay poster is written to cache/shared and shared from there, so another
  app receiving the intent can read that one picture and nothing else this app
  has on disk — not the audio cache, not the downloads, not the listening
  history. The in-app updater's APK cache is shared the same way, and only to
  the installer. A provider declared over the whole cache directory would work
  identically today and be a much larger promise.
-->
<paths>
    <cache-path name="shared" path="shared/" />
    <cache-path name="updates" path="updates/" />
</paths>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  The 4×1 entry in the widget picker: a capsule with a round cover, the track,
  and Like / previous / play / next / Shuffle. Its own provider and layout, not
  another size of MediaWidget — it has no full-bleed artwork, so none of that
  widget's measuring or blur applies.

  One row by the launcher's 70n − 30 arithmetic is 40dp, which is the minimum
  asked for; the capsule is wrap_content and centred in whatever the row really
  is. Resizable horizontally only, and not below three cells: the title and five
  buttons need that much before the buttons crowd.
-->
<appwidget-provider xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:description="@string/widget_pill_description"
    android:initialLayout="@layout/widget_media_pill"
    android:minHeight="40dp"
    android:minResizeWidth="180dp"
    android:minWidth="250dp"
    android:previewImage="@drawable/widget_preview_pill"
    android:previewLayout="@layout/widget_media_pill_preview"
    android:resizeMode="horizontal"
    android:targetCellHeight="1"
    android:targetCellWidth="4"
    android:updatePeriodMillis="0"
    android:widgetCategory="home_screen" />

app/src/main/res/xml/widget_media_square.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  The 2×2 entry in the widget picker. Sizes follow the launcher grid's own
  arithmetic — a span of n cells is 70n − 30 dp — so 2 cells is 110dp.

  resizeMode is horizontal only: every size this widget is meant to take is two
  rows tall, and the band at its foot is a fixed height, so a widget stretched
  vertically would just be more artwork above an unchanged bar. Width is free
  between two and four cells, and the layout swaps at
  MediaWidget.WIDE_LAYOUT_MIN_DP, so growing this one all the way picks up the
  4×2's own layout rather than leaving three buttons adrift in a wide band.

  maxResizeWidth is 288dp rather than 4 cells' nominal 250dp on purpose: cells
  are not really 70dp on every launcher, and a cap set at the nominal figure
  stops a launcher with slightly wider cells one column short of the four the
  widget is supposed to reach. 288dp clears four cells anywhere while staying
  well under five (320dp nominal), so the range on offer is the intended one.

  previewLayout points at a copy of the real layout carrying stand-in text, for
  the same reason the 4×2's does: widget_art holds no bitmap until a provider
  fills one in, so the root's gradient shows through and the picker sees a cover
  with the transport on it — but the title would be blank. previewImage is the
  fallback for hosts below API 31, which don't inflate previewLayout at all.
-->
<appwidget-provider xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:description="@string/widget_square_description"
    android:initialLayout="@layout/widget_media_compact"
    android:maxResizeWidth="288dp"
    android:minHeight="110dp"
    android:minResizeWidth="110dp"
    android:minWidth="110dp"
    android:previewImage="@drawable/widget_preview_square"
    android:previewLayout="@layout/widget_media_compact_preview"
    android:resizeMode="horizontal"
    android:targetCellHeight="2"
    android:targetCellWidth="2"
    android:updatePeriodMillis="0"
    android:widgetCategory="home_screen" />

package com.music.bitchord

import com.music.bitchord.data.LocalGroups
import com.music.bitchord.data.model.BrowseType
import com.music.bitchord.data.model.Song
import com.music.bitchord.download.DownloadedCollection
import com.music.bitchord.download.Downloads
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertNull
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

class LocalGroupsTest {

    private fun song(id: String, title: String, artist: String = "Artist", album: String? = "Album", track: Int? = null) =
        Song(videoId = id, title = title, artist = artist, thumbnailUrl = null, albumName = album, trackNumber = track)

    @Test
    fun pageIds_roundTripNamesWithColons() {
        val id = LocalGroups.albumPageId("local:downloads", "Live: At The Hall")
        assertEquals("local:downloads", LocalGroups.folderOf(id))
        assertEquals(BrowseType.ALBUM, LocalGroups.typeOf(id))
        assertFalse(LocalGroups.isArtist(id))

        val artist = LocalGroups.artistPageId("local:all", "AC/DC")
        assertEquals("local:all", LocalGroups.folderOf(artist))
        assertEquals(BrowseType.OTHER, LocalGroups.typeOf(artist))
        assertTrue(LocalGroups.isArtist(artist))
    }

    @Test
    fun folderOf_ignoresEverythingElse() {
        assertNull(LocalGroups.folderOf("local:downloads"))
        assertNull(LocalGroups.folderOf(Downloads.pageIdFor("MPREb_x")))
        assertNull(LocalGroups.folderOf("local:group:bogus:all:x"))
        assertNull(LocalGroups.folderOf(null))
    }

    @Test
    fun songsOf_rebuildsTheGroupInReleaseOrder() {
        val folder = listOf(
            song("b", "B", album = "Live: At The Hall", track = 2),
            song("x", "X", album = "Other"),
            song("a", "A", album = "Live: At The Hall", track = 1),
        )
        val id = LocalGroups.albumPageId("local:all", "Live: At The Hall")
        assertEquals(listOf("a", "b"), LocalGroups.songsOf(id, folder).map { it.videoId })
    }

    @Test
    fun albumsOf_namedReleaseWinsOverItsOwnTags() {
        val tracks = listOf(song("a", "A", album = "Record"), song("b", "B", album = "Tagged"))
        val downloaded = DownloadedCollection(
            id = "MPREb_1",
            title = "record",
            subtitle = "",
            thumbnailUrl = "art",
            playlist = false,
            songs = listOf(tracks[0]),
        )
        val albums = LocalGroups.albumsOf("local:downloads", tracks, listOf(downloaded))
        assertEquals(listOf("record", "Tagged"), albums.map { it.title })
        assertEquals(Downloads.pageIdFor("MPREb_1"), albums[0].browseId)
        assertEquals("MPREb_1", albums[0].downloadId)
        assertEquals("Artist", albums[0].subtitle)
        assertNull(albums[1].downloadId)
    }

    private fun file(id: String, title: String, path: String?) =
        Song(videoId = id, title = title, artist = "Artist", thumbnailUrl = null, localUri = "content://$id", localPath = path)

    @Test
    fun directoryPageIds_roundTripPaths() {
        val id = LocalGroups.directoryPageId("local:all", "/storage/emulated/0/Music/Live: 2019")
        assertEquals("local:all", LocalGroups.folderOf(id))
        assertEquals(BrowseType.PLAYLIST, LocalGroups.typeOf(id))
        assertTrue(LocalGroups.isDirectory(id))
        assertFalse(LocalGroups.isArtist(id))
        assertFalse(LocalGroups.isDirectory(LocalGroups.albumPageId("local:all", "Live: 2019")))
    }

    @Test
    fun foldersOf_groupsByDirectoryAndSkipsPathless() {
        val tracks = listOf(
            file("b", "B", "/storage/emulated/0/Music/Rock/b.mp3"),
            file("a", "A", "/storage/emulated/0/Music/Rock/a.mp3"),
            file("c", "C", "/storage/1A2B-3C4D/Music/c.flac"),
            file("d", "D", "/storage/emulated/0/Download/d.mp3"),
            file("x", "X", null),
        )
        val folders = LocalGroups.foldersOf("local:all", tracks)
        assertEquals(listOf("Download", "Music", "Rock"), folders.map { it.title })
        assertEquals(listOf("", "1A2B-3C4D", "Music"), folders.map { it.subtitle })
        val rock = folders.last()
        assertEquals(listOf("a", "b"), rock.songs.map { it.videoId })
        // The page reads the same rows back off a fresh listing.
        assertEquals(listOf("a", "b"), LocalGroups.songsOf(rock.browseId, tracks).map { it.videoId })
    }
}

package com.music.bitchord

import com.music.bitchord.download.OfflineDash
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

/**
 * The MPD reader, against the manifests that actually reach a download.
 *
 * Worth testing at this level because the failure it replaces was silent: a
 * `.mpd` used to be fetched as though it were audio and written into a file
 * named `.flac`, and nothing anywhere said so — the download reported success
 * and the 2.7 KB result simply refused to play. A parser that drops the last
 * segment or overstates a duration fails the same quiet way, so the numbers
 * below are checked against a real Tidal manifest rather than a made-up one.
 */
class OfflineDashTest {

    private companion object {
        /**
         * Tidal's manifest for The Weeknd's "Starboy" at `quality=LOSSLESS`,
         * September 2026, with the signed CloudFront URLs shortened. Everything
         * that matters to the reader — the timeline, the timescale, the
         * `$Number$` template and the escaped `&` in the query — is
         * verbatim.
         */
        const val STARBOY = """<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?><MPD xmlns="urn:mpeg:dash:schema:mpd:2011" """ +
            """profiles="urn:mpeg:dash:profile:isoff-main:2011" type="static" minBufferTime="PT3.993S" """ +
            """mediaPresentationDuration="PT3M50.461S"><Period id="0"><AdaptationSet id="0" contentType="audio" """ +
            """mimeType="audio/mp4" lang="und" group="main" segmentAlignment="true">""" +
            """<Representation id="FLAC,44100,16" codecs="flac" bandwidth="928340" audioSamplingRate="44100">""" +
            """<SegmentTemplate timescale="44100" """ +
            """initialization="https://sp-ad-cf.audio.tidal.com/mediatracks/BLOB/0.mp4?Policy=P&Signature=S" """ +
            """media="https://sp-ad-cf.audio.tidal.com/mediatracks/BLOB/${'$'}Number${'$'}.mp4?Policy=P&Signature=S" """ +
            """startNumber="1"><SegmentTimeline><S d="176128" r="56"/><S d="124050"/></SegmentTimeline>""" +
            """</SegmentTemplate></Representation></AdaptationSet></Period></MPD>"""
    }

    @Test
    fun `a manifest is recognised by its extension, query string and all`() {
        assertTrue(OfflineDash.handles("https://im-cf.manifest.tidal.com/1/manifests/AbC.mpd?Expires=1&Signature=x"))
        assertTrue(OfflineDash.handles("https://host/a.MPD"))
        assertFalse(OfflineDash.handles("https://im-cf.manifest.tidal.com/1/manifests/AbC.m3u8?Expires=1"))
        assertFalse(OfflineDash.handles("https://aac.saavncdn.com/820/abc_320.mp4"))
    }

    /**
     * `r` counts *repeats*, not segments, so `r="56"` is 57 of them. Read as a
     * count it silently truncates every download by one segment — four seconds
     * of the end of the song, on a file that otherwise looks complete.
     */
    @Test
    fun `the timeline expands to one entry per segment`() {
        val plan = OfflineDash.parse(STARBOY)
        assertEquals(58, plan.media.size)
        assertEquals(58, plan.seconds.size)

        // 57 full segments at 176128/44100, then a short one at 124050/44100.
        assertEquals(3.994, plan.seconds.first(), 0.001)
        assertEquals(3.994, plan.seconds[56], 0.001)
        assertEquals(2.813, plan.seconds.last(), 0.001)

        // And they add up to the runtime the manifest states, which is the one
        // number that catches an off-by-one anywhere in the expansion.
        assertEquals(230.461, plan.seconds.sum(), 0.01)
    }

    /**
     * `$Number$` starts at `startNumber`, and the initialisation segment is a
     * separate URL rather than number zero — getting that wrong fetches the
     * init segment twice and loses the last one.
     */
    @Test
    fun `segment urls come off the template unescaped`() {
        val plan = OfflineDash.parse(STARBOY)
        assertEquals("https://sp-ad-cf.audio.tidal.com/mediatracks/BLOB/0.mp4?Policy=P&Signature=S", plan.initialization)
        assertEquals("https://sp-ad-cf.audio.tidal.com/mediatracks/BLOB/1.mp4?Policy=P&Signature=S", plan.media.first())
        assertEquals("https://sp-ad-cf.audio.tidal.com/mediatracks/BLOB/58.mp4?Policy=P&Signature=S", plan.media.last())
    }

    /**

        )
    }
